key_insight: Introduce and analyze 'symbolic properties'—state-set predicates that capture behavioral guarantees of DRL agents across ranges of system states—allowing verification and reasoning beyond single input points. This yields broader, more practical assurances for DRL in systems and networking.
problem_solved: Existing verification approaches for DRL in systems and networking focus on pointwise properties (fixed inputs) and thus provide limited coverage; this paper addresses the challenge of specifying and checking richer, range-based properties that better reflect real-world state variability.
method: Formalize symbolic properties as predicates or constraints over sets of environment/system states that express safety, performance, or invariants for DRL agents.

Develop a verification/analysis workflow that checks these symbolic properties (via symbolic reasoning, over-approximation, or targeted testing) and produces counterexamples or certificates when a property fails.

Evaluate the approach on representative systems-and-networking tasks (e.g., adaptive streaming, wireless resource allocation, congestion control) to demonstrate improved coverage and actionable diagnostics.
impact: Provides practitioners tools to specify meaningful, range-based guarantees for deployed DRL controllers, improving trust, safety, and diagnosability in critical networking and systems applications. It bridges the gap between formal verification and practical robustness testing for learned policies.
visual_elements: State-space diagram showing a symbolic property as a shaded region and agent trajectories entering/exiting that region (illustrates range-based guarantees vs. point checks).
Pipeline flowchart: property specification → symbolic analyzer/ verifier → counterexample / certificate → policy refinement (shows method at a glance).
Heatmap or bar chart comparing coverage and failure modes of pointwise verification vs. symbolic-property analysis across networking benchmarks.
Icon set: network/device icons (streaming, base station, router) linked to property badges (safety, throughput, latency) to highlight application domains and guarantees.
paper_title: Analyzing Symbolic Properties for DRL Agents in Systems and Networking
paper_authors: Mohammad Zangooei, Jannis Weil, Amr Rizk, Mina Tahmasbi Arashloo, Raouf Boutaba
